# Model overview

**MOOOD** is an open-source discrete-event simulation developed by Richard Pilbery and colleagues. It follows callers after an NHS 111 primary-care disposition and represents subsequent contact with primary care, NHS 111, ambulance services and emergency departments. The Python and SimPy model compares the existing system with timely primary-care contact and reports activity across services and avoidable ED attendance.

The original data and parameters relate to callers registered with Bradford and Airedale GP practices, so reuse elsewhere requires local review and validation.

## Actions for participants before the session

Open the [MOOOD repository](https://github.com/ReModel-Club/MOOOD-study) and follow the setup instructions. Participants should aim to:

<!---
- Follow the [generated documentation](https://richardpilbery.github.io/MOOOD-study/) and repository setup instructions as far as you can.
-->
- Clone the repository and follow the setup instructions in the README to get the model running locally.
- Read the abstract and strengths and limitations in the [BMJ Open paper](https://bmjopen.bmj.com/content/13/9/e076203).

Alternatively, participants can use [CodeSpaces](https://github.com/codespaces) to explore the model without a local installation (see README for details). The aim is for participants to come to the session with a successful model run that they can continue to explore.

## Session objectives and outline

This session will focus on discussing how participants experienced getting the model running. Participants will:

- discuss any issues they encountered and how they resolved them;
- share their experience of running the model and interpreting the outputs;
- discuss what they learned from attempting to reproduce an existing model
